text: Half mad with fear. <break time="0.8s" /> I rushed into the great hall. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the little people were sleeping. <break time="0.8s" /> And woke them. <break time="0.8s" /> By shouting and striking a match. <break time="0.8s" /> A few of them laughed. <break time="0.8s" /> But most of them. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked terribly frightened. <break time="0.8s" /> And they ran away from me. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> Exhausted at last. <break time="0.8s" /> I fell asleep on the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the sphinx. <break time="0.8s" /> And when I woke up. <break time="0.8s" /> It was already morning. <break time="0.8s" /> In the calm light of day. <break time="0.8s" /> I could think clearly. <break time="0.8s" /> And I knew. <break time="0.8s" /> That the machine could not have traveled in time. <break time="0.8s" /> Without its levers. <break time="0.8s" /> Then I found a groove. <break time="0.8s" /> Torn in the grass. <break time="0.8s" /> With strange narrow footprints beside it. <break time="0.8s" /> Which led straight. <break time="0.8s" /> To the bronze pedestal of the sphinx. <break time="0.8s" /> The pedestal had panels of bronze. <break time="0.8s" /> On its sides. <break time="0.8s" /> But there were no handles or keyholes. <break time="0.8s" /> And the panels would not move at all. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked the little people by signs. <break time="0.8s" /> To open the panels. <break time="0.8s" /> They turned away from me. <break time="0.8s" /> As if I had done something shameful. <break time="0.8s" /> Patience I told myself. <break time="0.8s" /> For the only way to get my machine back. <break time="0.8s" /> Was to learn the secrets. <break time="0.8s" /> Of this strange world. <break time="0.8s" /> A few days later. <break time="0.8s" /> I saved a little girl named Weena. <break time="0.8s" /> From drowning. <break time="0.8s" /> And from then on she followed me everywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a gentle friend.
